correctness.rationale: The 2-by-2 matrix determinant and cross-resolvent identity give an exact normalized trace ratio; the scalar envelope gives existence and strict increase. A uniform O(delta) expansion of the singular integral after subtraction yields the delta log(1/delta) boundary term. Maximizers stay compact and converge to the unique scalar optimizer, justifying taking the sharp supremum. A distinct eigenbasis divided-difference computation checked nine matrix examples; six asymptotic tests corroborate but do not prove the limit. Domain is 1/2<alpha<1, 0<t<=1, nonzero rank-one inputs, no zero denominator.

originality.rationale: Theorem 4 in arXiv:2610.39598 proves an unconditional bound, and sharpness is witnessed by fully aligned matrices. It does not determine a fixed nonparallel overlap optimal coefficient or quantify its singular alignment deficit. Exact two-dimensional resolvent and uniform boundary-layer calculation provide information not implied by the unconditional coefficient. Semantic searches of published mathematical literature and primary text did not locate an equivalent; novelty is assessed only to best knowledge.

value.rationale: The exact best tilting coefficient under fixed pure-state squared overlap is a geometrically natural quantum-information invariant not determined by the sharp unrestricted inequality. Strictly improved constants quantify nonparallel rank-one behavior and the positive leading logarithmic cusp identifies a nonanalytic stability law approaching aligned extremizers. This motivates an independently useful family of sharp tests for operator inequalities; no universal high-rank stability theorem is claimed.
